orgs.name: ALLIANCE HEALTHCARE SERVICES INC
services: Memphis' largest nonprofit behavioral health provider (org's own description): outpatient mental health care for adults, children and families - counseling, psychiatry, peer support - at 8 clinic locations across Shelby County, sliding scale, no one turned away for inability to pay
Addiction recovery treatment: counseling, psychiatry and peer support

24/7 crisis services: Crisis Wellness Center, 3200 Broad Avenue (45 beds; crisis stabilization, respite and medically monitored detox; walk-in, no appointment or insurance required) and Children & Youth Crisis Wellness Center, 602 Malcomb St (ages 4-17, opened June 1 2026); 24/7 crisis line (901) 577-9400; mobile crisis and pre-arrest diversion
orgs.serves: adults, children and families in Memphis and Shelby County needing mental health, addiction or crisis care

orgs.name: ALPHA OMEGA VETERANS SERVICES INC
services: Housing for veterans: capacity to house over 120 veterans (male and female), in programs from 30 days to 2 years aimed at reintegration and placement into permanent housing
Integrated services at its facilities: food, clothing, housing, transportation and rehabilitation assistance

Intensive individual and group counseling for combat/service-related conditions including PTSD, anger management, substance abuse and other mental health disorders; help securing military service-related benefits; career assessments, job search and training assistance
orgs.serves: military veterans in Memphis and Shelby County, including veterans in recovery/rehabilitation

orgs.name: CATHOLIC CHARITIES OF THE DIOCESE OF MEMPHIS INC
services: Emergency Services: food, clothing, hygiene products and other basic essentials, distributed on-site and by mobile distribution (org reports 50,000+ unduplicated individuals served across West Tennessee)

Housing Services: assistance for people experiencing homelessness aimed at permanent, stable housing; veteran services incl. the St. Sebastian Veteran Services program; Genesis Homeless Services (HUD CoC-funded, FY2024)
Outreach Services for Memphis' homeless population: mobile street outreach, daily meals, clothing, restrooms and hand-washing stations
Community Support Services: food support for children in poverty; Tiny Blessings diapers/essentials for mothers and caregivers of infants through age 3
orgs.serves: low-income households, people experiencing homelessness, disaster victims, veterans, and families with young children in Memphis / West Tennessee

orgs.name: CHURCH HEALTH CENTER OF MEMPHIS INC
services: Quality, affordable health care for uninsured, underserved people and their families at 1350 Concourse Ave, Suite 142, Memphis: medical clinic on a sliding scale based on income and family size
Dental clinic, eye care clinic, family care & pediatrics, behavioral health services (counseling and social services support), physical rehabilitation and pharmacy access for Church Health patients
Urgent care clinic (call 901-272-0003 for an appointment); established patients register by phone with photo ID, proof of address and proof of income if uninsured
orgs.serves: working, uninsured and underinsured Memphians and their families, all ages

orgs.name: COMMUNITY ALLIANCE FOR THE HOMELESS INC
services: Memphis/Shelby County Continuum of Care (TN-501) lead agency and HMIS lead - the community's front door system for homelessness assistance

Coordinated Entry System (CES): people in a housing crisis are assessed at designated CES access points (equipped with HMIS/CES training) and entered into CES; CAFTH coordinates CES operations, manages housing matches and monitors vacancies (CAFTH CES Policy & Procedure Manual, Nov 2024). All CoC, YHDP and ESG funded programs (PSH, rapid rehousing, SSVF) must participate in CES
Population-specific CES By-Name Lists (incl. family, youth and domestic-violence CES streams) and YHDP youth navigation
orgs.serves: people experiencing or at risk of homelessness in Memphis and Shelby County

orgs.name: DOOR OF HOPE INC
services: Permanent and supportive housing for Memphis' most vulnerable people experiencing homelessness, in guests' own apartments or in one of Door of Hope's three facilities
Supportive services aimed at keeping guests housed and helping them reach independence, self-determination and personal responsibility
Housing programs for survivors of domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault and stalking (incl. HUD CoC-funded Door of Hope DV)
orgs.serves: people experiencing homelessness, particularly those living with serious mental illness, substance use disorders and/or chronic health conditions, and survivors of domestic violence - Memphis

orgs.name: HABITAT FOR HUMANITY INTERNATIONAL INC
services: Partners with Memphis and Shelby County residents to build or improve homes: new home construction and rehabilitation, with affordable (zero-interest) mortgages for first-time homebuyers

Aging In Place (AIP) Program: mobility/accessibility modifications and critical home repairs for older homeowners (62+, City of Memphis, income at or below 50% AMI; pre-application by hotline only, 901-322-3500)
orgs.serves: low-to-moderate income homebuyers and older homeowners in Memphis and Shelby County

orgs.name: HOSPITALITY HUB OF MEMPHIS
services: Single point of entry to comprehensive support services for people experiencing homelessness in downtown Memphis (590 Washington Ave): Guest Services Mon-Fri 9am-noon and 1-3pm
Hub Hotel: free, barrier-free emergency shelter for women (including trans women) and their accompanying children, open 24/7, with three meals a day, laundry and case counselors

Help acquiring identification, employment opportunities and referrals to community partners; Hub Hall transitional housing for young adults 18-24 via a Youth Navigator; Hub Studios temporary shelter for guests other options cannot serve
orgs.serves: any individual experiencing homelessness in Memphis; Hub Hotel serves women and their children

orgs.name: MEMPHIS AREA INTERGROUP ASSOCIATION OF ALCOHOLICS ANONYMOUS
services: The official AA meeting list for the Memphis area - in-person and online meetings with a find-a-meeting search on the intergroup's own site (memphis-aa.org)
24-hour helpline: (901) 454-1414 (published on the intergroup's own site)
Intergroup office: 3540 Summer Avenue, Suite 104, Memphis TN 38122 (directory listings for the intergroup)
orgs.serves: people seeking recovery from alcoholism in Memphis and Shelby County (the intergroup also lists some meetings across the river in MS/AR - those meetings are outside this county pilot and are not separately listed)

orgs.name: MEMPHIS AREA LEGAL SERVICES ASSOC
services: Free legal advice and representation for low-income, disabled and elderly clients in legal crises that threaten self-sufficiency or quality of life - MALS never charges for its services
General Sessions Courthouse Clinic (Room 119, 140 Adams Avenue, Memphis) and periodic Saturday clinics

Case types documented across its own site and the Memphis Bar listing: housing/eviction and foreclosure prevention, family law and orders of protection, consumer/debt, public benefits, tax controversies, and legal help for veterans (SSVF legal-services history - see fiscal map)
orgs.serves: low-income, disabled and elderly residents of Shelby, Fayette, Lauderdale and Tipton counties (org's own site)

orgs.name: MEMPHIS UNION MISSION
services: Men's Emergency Shelter, 383 Poplar Ave, Memphis: overnight shelter; breakfast, lunch and dinner (lunch served daily to men who check in for the day; dinner and breakfast for overnight guests)
Clothes closet (free clothing) and hot showers with soap and shampoo for homeless guests
Free medical clinic for people experiencing homelessness, Mondays and Thursdays, with Christ Community Health Services and Baptist Memorial Healthcare

Iron-on-Iron Recovery Program: one-year intensive residential, Christ-centered recovery program for men (three phases at Memphis-area locations, starting at the Men's Emergency Shelter); Moriah House is the Mission's long-term recovery program for women and their children
orgs.serves: men, women and families experiencing homelessness, addiction and crisis in Memphis

orgs.name: METROPOLITAN INTER-FAITH ASSOC
services: Emergency shelter for families: online application on MIFA's own site; staff respond within 24 hours (MIFA Housing Stability Programs)

Emergency Services: emergency rent, mortgage and utility assistance for Shelby County households that have suffered a documented crisis (MIFA partners with MLGW in the Plus-1 utility assistance program)
Meals on Wheels and senior independence programs; MIFA also serves as central intake for the Memphis/Shelby County Emergency Housing Partnership (per MLGW's spotlight on MIFA)
orgs.serves: vulnerable seniors and families in crisis in Memphis and Shelby County

orgs.name: MID-SOUTH FOOD BANK
services: Regional food bank: collects and distributes wholesome food through a network of partner agencies - food pantries, soup kitchens, shelters, youth and senior programs - across its Mid-South service area including Shelby County
Mobile Pantry: direct food distributions in underserved areas using refrigerated vehicles (schedule on the org's Find Food page)
Feeding Children programs: Kids Cafe free hot meals, Food for Kids BackPack weekend food, and School Pantries; Feeding Seniors: Senior Nutrition boxes and No Hungry Seniors discharge/waitlist food
orgs.serves: people facing hunger in Shelby County and the wider Mid-South (12 TN, 18 MS, 1 AR counties)

orgs.name: NARCOTICS ANONYMOUS - WEST TENNESSEE AREA
services: The West Tennessee Area of NA maintains the Memphis-area NA meeting schedule on its own site (na-wt.org) - meetings across Memphis and Shelby County
NA helpline: (901) 276-5483 (published on the area's own site)
orgs.serves: people seeking recovery from drug addiction in Memphis, Shelby County and West Tennessee

orgs.name: ROOM IN THE INN - MEMPHIS
services: Free seasonal congregational overnight shelter: seven nights a week in winter (Nov 1 - Mar 31) and reduced nights in summer (May 1 - Sep 30), hosted by local faith communities; guests receive a meal and a safe place to sleep
Guest registration 4:30-5:00pm on shelter days at First Presbyterian Church, 166 Poplar Avenue; priority to families with children, then single women; transport to and from host sites
Also operates a Family Inn and a Recuperative Care Center (org's own site)
orgs.serves: families with children and individuals experiencing homelessness in Memphis

orgs.name: SHELBY COUNTY COMMUNITY SERVICES AGENCY (CSA)
services: Comprehensive Emergency Assistance Program (CEAP): rent or mortgage assistance that helps prevent evictions and foreclosures - for Shelby County residents behind on payment after a job loss/income reduction or documented unexpected expense in the last 4 months; approved payments go directly to the landlord or mortgage company (Shelby County's own CSA FAQ)

LIHEAP (Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program): utility/energy assistance for eligible Shelby County households, incl. crisis help - CSA is the county's LIHEAP agency (FY2025 application published on CSA's own site; THDA program year)

Medical prescription assistance and supportive services/case management (CSA's own customer survey lists Rent/Mortgage Assistance, Utilities Assistance, Eviction Prevention Program, Medical Prescription Assistance and Supportive Services/Case Management)
orgs.serves: low-income households in Shelby County facing eviction, foreclosure or energy shutoff

orgs.name: THE SALVATION ARMY - MEMPHIS AREA COMMAND (PURDUE CENTER OF HOPE / ADULT REHABILITATION CENTER)
services: Purdue Center of Hope, 696 Jackson Ave, Memphis - the largest provider of shelter and services to homeless women and children in Memphis (org's own history page): AutoZone Single Women's Residence with individual case management, housing and employment assistance

New Directions Family Residence: emergency services for up to 90 days for mothers and children experiencing poverty and homelessness, with the Pathway of Hope program (up to one year: employment education, debt resolution, parenting and life skills)
Renewal Place Family Residence: up to two-year program for women facing addiction and their children - treatment, trauma repair therapy and case management while families stay together
Intensive Outpatient Program (IOP): 12-step, abstinence-based group and individual counseling for addiction recovery

Adult Rehabilitation Center (Mid-South ARC), 2649 Kirby Whitten: residential work-therapy program (140 men working toward sobriety and rehabilitation, supported by Family Stores); combined with Renewal Place and IOP, the org describes itself as Memphis' largest provider of alcohol and drug recovery programs
orgs.serves: women and children experiencing homelessness, single women, and men and women in addiction recovery - Memphis and the Mid-South
